newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila buys more China, Vietnam rice below $290/T.
newsitem.headline: Manila buys more China, Vietnam rice below $290/T.

text.p: The additional 150,000 tonnes of rice bought by the Philippines from Vietnam and China last week was priced at below $290 per tonne C&F, an official at the Agriculture Department said on Monday.

Last week, state-owned National Food Authority (NFA) said it will use its option to buy 100,000 tonnes of rice from Vietnam and 50,000 tonnes from China to complete its procurement programme before July this year.
The new orders were on top of previous contracts made by the NFA for 100,000 tonnes each from China and Vietnam at $291.50 per tonne C&F.
President Fidel Ramos has authorised the NFA to import up to 650,000 tonnes of rice from neighbouring countries to beef up the country's buffer stocks before July this year.
Philippine rice harvests in the third quarter are traditionally low.
Besides Vietnam and China, the NFA also contracted for 205,000 tonnes of rice from Thailand at $300 per tonne C&F, and 100,000 tonnes from Malaysia at $291.50 per tonne C&F.
